articleTitle: Algorithm of signal processing in ultra-wideband radar designed for remote measuring parameters of patient's cardiac activity
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The algorithm of processing the data received from the medical ultra-wideband (UWB) radar is described. The algorithm provides a possible of comparing the results of heart activity monitoring performed by the UWB radar with indications from the electrocardiograph and making a conclusion about the opportunity of using the similar equipment in medical institutions.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband radar
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Here, we present a description of a block scheme, characteristics, specific features of design and results of testing for a prototype of the ultrawideband (UWB) radar, which has been developed by Russian UWB group researchers at Moscow Aviation Institute at "analog and digital radio systems" department (www.uwbgroup.ru). The prototype was designed within a research work, which we are conducting on the state order from one of Russian federation state institutions. The UWB radar is intended for detection of moving targets at a distance of several kilometers. The radar design is divided into two stages. In the first stage, we have produced a radar prototype, which incorporates a low power narrow-pulse generator (NPG). During laboratory test, the prototype has afforded the detection of moving targets at the distance of up to one hundred meters. Thereby, the validity of technical solutions used for the whole radar's and radar unit's design was confirmed. In the second stage, we plan to conduct field tests of the radar prototype equipped with a high power NPG.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband radar for remote detection and measurement of parameters of the moving objects on small range
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Consideration is given to methods of designing ultrawide band (UWB) radars intended for detection and remote measuring parameters of moving objects at short distances (tens of centimeters-units of meters). The descriptions of radar's structure schemes and characteristics are given together with main results of prototype test. The analysis of fields of application for UWB radars demonstrates that radars of that type can be used practically in all cases where we need highly precise remote observation of moving objects at short distances.

articleTitle: UWB radar high resolution ISAR imaging
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Are presented results of high-resolution ISAR imaging using ultra wide band radar system working in time domain. Experiment was done in the ordinary room. Image resolution was 1 mm. Results are important for various applications.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband systems-features and ways of development
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Consideration is given to the main specific features of ultrawideband (UWB) systems and possibilities of these systems to increase essentially the information performance of radars and communication. The problem of particular interest is the difference in constructions between UWB and conventional radar systems operating in a narrow frequency band. The difficulties caused by these differences when constructing UWB systems are determined. Also discussed are the ways to counter these difficulties, which makes it possible to expand the UWB radar application area and realize the advantage over conventional radar systems.

articleTitle: Signal processing in UWB radars of small distance
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: In the paper, the methods of signal processing with reference to ultrawide band (UWB) radars designed for detection and remote measuring parameters of moving objects at short ranges (tens of centimeters-several meters) are considered. It is shown that the relative changes of an oscillation frequency filling an outgoing pulse and duration of these pulses originating at reflection from a moving target are very small; that makes impossible their practical measurement. Therefore, for detection of signals reflected from a moving target the phase method is chosen.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic impulse radiator
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: A novel method of short electromagnetic pulse producing by electrical dipole antenna is a topic of this paper. This method assumes the antenna current interruption instead of voltage pulse excitation. In this case antenna-generator matching requirements are considerable simplified and antenna radiation efficiency is increased. In according to proposed method the electromagnetic impulse radiator prototype was developed. Antenna current is interrupted by a drift step recovery diode (DSRD), and antenna is a part of the DSRD generator itself. More than 800 watts peak power was achieved on the antenna terminal with 3 ns monocycle pulse duration and up to 250 kHz pulse repetition frequency (PRF). The radiator power consumption didn't exceed 3 watts at 100 kHz PRF condition. The proposed method allows producing of nanosecond electromagnetic pulses with hundred kilowatts peak power and PRF up to hundreds kHz. Only switch parameters and power supply limit potential possibilities of such kind of radiator

articleTitle: Differential switched oscillators and associated antennas. Part 2
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Building on previous results, switched oscillators and associated antennas are extended to new variations. Differential systems are considered with inline differential oscillators near the reflector focus for the purpose of increasing the voltage delivered to the antenna and thereby the far field. This leads to the concept of a separated reflector with two ground planes, two separated reflector foci, and a space between the ground planes for placing pulse-power equipment.

articleTitle: Natural resonance frequency extraction using an early-time and late-time responses combined technique
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: A pole extraction method using an early-time and late-time responses combined technique is presented. Without the determination of the beginning of the target transient response, the proposed method assumes an ARMA representation to approximate the complete target transient response, and a total least square method is applied to poles extraction. The proposed method is validated using a measured scattering data of a thin wire and a finite cylinder. The processing results show that the proposed method is superior to the KT method and matrix pencil method in an appropriate SNR.

articleTitle: The automatic determination of soil permittivity using the response from a subsurface local object
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The method for determining permittivity of soil containing a local object is proposed. The method based on the Hough transform is one of effective means to detect hyperbolic reflections from such objects on the GPR profile image. On the basis of the same method the iterative algorithm, which allows automatic determination of exact value of permittivity of ground using the results of subsurface radiolocation, has been developed. Its efficiency is shown using the simulated GPR profile example.

articleTitle: The scope of application of a reciprocity principle in the theory of antennas at radiation and reception of ultra-wideband signals
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: An antenna for a reception of the signals, which have spatial length much less than physical length of the antenna and the processes occurring in this antenna, are considered. On an example of the elementary antenna-the symmetric vibrator-features of ultra-wideband (UWB) signals reception are shown and dependence of a current's form in loading of the antenna from a positional relationship of transmitting and reception antennas is described. It is shown, that change of the form of a field of transmitting antenna from change of a positional relationship of antennas does not allow using a reciprocity principle for construction of the reception antenna's pattern. Physical interpretation of the processes occurring in the antenna is given. The field's pattern is given at excitation of the antenna by the UWB signal. Nonstationary character of these diagrams is shown. As the basic characteristic of the UWB antenna for practical appendices the pattern on energy is considered.

articleTitle: A UWB impulse surface penetrating radar system for pavement evaluation
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: An advanced UWB impulse surface penetrating radar (SPR) system-RadarEye is introduced in This work. It provides high resolution pavement thickness estimation and subsurface objects imaging for civil structures inspection. Super resolution time delay estimation algorithm based on wavelet transform and TAM-BP imaging algorithm are presented with high accuracy on layer thickness estimation and high spatial resolution on subsurface imaging. Both indoor and outdoor experiments show the feasibility of this system.

articleTitle: CPW to CPS transition for feeding UWB antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The paper considers a transition (balun) from coplanar waveguide (CPW) to coplanar stripline (CPS) which is nonresonant and suitable for feeding UWB antennas such as tapered slot antennas (Vivaldi antennas in particular), bow-tie antennas and other. Some numerical and experimental results are presented that show performance of the transition alone and as a feeder for a Vivaldi antenna.

articleTitle: Fractal ultra-wideband signals
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The fractal ultra-wideband (FUWB) signals as a new type of the ultra-wideband (UWB) signals for application in different branches of science and engineering in particular for near-to-Earth space investigations are proposed. Different characteristics of new analytical and numerical models of FUWB signals with using of the Fourier-and wavelet analysis are investigated. The wavelet analysis is proposed to apply for detection of FUWB signals against an interference background.

articleTitle: An experimental UWB module-based sensing and communication system
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: An experimental UWB system is developed, designed, prototyped and tested to support a number of multitask sensing and telecommunication applications in the 0.1-3.0 GHz band, viz. subsurface radar or GPR, intrusion sensor, "trough-wall seeing" scanner, indoor comm. & geolocation and so on. As such, a set of hardware modules has to be created that can be combined/assembled in a particular fashion/architecture for each specific mission including functioning with receiving and transmitting UWB arrays (a part of our ongoing R&D efforts). The basic system components involve: (1) transmitter (Tx), (2) receiver (Rx), (4) antennas, (5) control unit, (6) digitizer and comp interface. As well, controlling and processing software is an inherent part of each such system that has to be configured for each specific operational task

articleTitle: Sensitivity of UWB ferrite receiving antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Dependence of sensitivity and degree of the shape distortion of the received signals on the antenna dimensions and the ferrite rod dimensions, on relative permeability of the ferrite rod, on the load resistance are investigated. Optimal dimensions and parameters of the receiving ferrite antenna providing the highest sensitivity under the condition of undistorted shape signal reception are determined.

articleTitle: Simulation of target detection using a high range resolution radar
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The use of wideband radar signals is sometimes more preferable for solving not only the tasks of target resolution, recognition, measurement, and the illumination stealth, but the traditional task of detection too. The latter is due to the decreased fluctuations of echoes. However, if the signal has an excessively wide bandwidth, the losses of noncoherent integration increase and the threshold signals rise. We investigate the detection threshold signals for the targets of different sizes, for illumination signals of various bandwidths, and for detection of different type.

articleTitle: A few examples of interferometry applications in space-related active and passive remote sensing
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The paper describes only a few examples of interferometry applications for space related active and passive remote sensing scenarios. Pulses with defined bandwidths as needed in a total system picture are applied (active remote sensing). Several accurate radar remote-sensing satellites have been produced under ESA's technical management. Work continues (www.esa.inQ) and new missions are developed. Also, such activities are ongoing at the level of National Space Agencies (Italy, Germany, etc.). Stability in instrumentation and related signal settings permits to make further advances and interferometry applications are advancing strongly. Some examples are shown, from which one observes, that accuracy is a very important factor. Ultra stabile reference clock signals are needed in interferometry applications with as an extreme example an experiment to perform Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) tracking of a weak transmission signal at Saturn's distance. Clock stability, using masers with 10"14 to 10"15 sec accuracy is needed here.

articleTitle: Wideband antenna measurements in anechoic chamber
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The method is considered which consists of measurements of output antenna signals on a number of frequencies and Fourier transformation of data into time domain for separation of own antenna field and interference fields. The results of testing at serial facility for antenna measurements in anechoic chamber are presented as for diagnosis of scattered fields, as for improvement of accuracy of antenna characteristics evaluation.

articleTitle: Wideband radar remote sensing of the atmosphere: a data interpretation problem
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Wideband radar application for the remote sensing of the atmosphere is considered. Features of distributed targets as objects of wideband radar observations are shown. The difficulties of the retrieval meteorological information from the returns are discussed. Prospect of UWB radar for remote sensing is reviewed.

articleTitle: The VIY-2 ground penetrating radar
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The VIY-2 ground penetrating radar (GPR) with unique sounding possibilities and use simplicity is presented at this paper. The VIY-2 GPR combines all units (synchronizer, transmitting and receiving modules, power supply and antenna system) into single case. The VIY-2 GPR communicates with computer via standard interface RS232 or USB 1.0. Utilized by the VIY-2 GPR technical solutions reduce deployment time and simplify survey process. The VIY-2 GPR design features and its components interaction are considered. Some field results are also presented. The VIY-2 GPR design concept allows reducing the data acquisition time, optimizing the time-varying gain control function, applying depth-stacking dependence, controlling the survey window position and interference reducing by pulse repetition frequency randomizing.

articleTitle: Application of radioabsorbing materials for the decision of a problem of the radioelectronic equipment compatibility
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Some ways of the decision of a problem of the radioelectronic equipment electromagnetic compatibility dealing with creation of new materials effectively interacting with electromagnetic irradiation (EMI) and special constructions based on it are designated There are presented some examples of last generation radioshielding and radioabsorbing materials of various classes with interesting both radiophysics and operational characteristics, have been design by authors. To achieve a good price/quality ratio and high efficiency it is necessary choice relevant type of microwave absorber material and construction for the current task, depending on concrete radiophysical and operational conditions of application. That's why "Radiostrim" company spent parallel development of several classes' materials. Each type of the listed materials possesses the advantages and lacks, accordingly, has the various cost price. The main concept of activity of our enterprise - to provide all spectrums of the microwave absorbers potentially required at the present stage development both in technological, and in financial and industrial aspect.

articleTitle: The influence of dielectric layer in waveguide on the characteristics of multislot antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: One of the ways to improve the properties of the scanning waveguide-slot antennas is a broadening of their frequency band. The aim of this work is to study the possibilities of the scanning waveguide-slot antennas characteristics improvement with the partial filling by dielectric, which makes it possible to slow down a wave in the waveguide and to broad it's frequency band with the inessential weight increasing.

articleTitle: Wideband radar (advantages and problems)
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Review of advantages and problems of wideband radar is given. Some criteria of wideband (UWB) radar are discussed to avoid misunderstanding when only the relative signal bandwidth is used as a criterion. Brief historical outline of the first and follow up experiments by different authors is presented. Advantages and disadvantages of bandwidth widening can be compared using the computer simulation of scattering. Experience of various simulation methods use, their applications to the target detection, tracking and recognition problems are briefly discussed and compared with experiment. Interference immunity, electromagnetic compatibility, stealth of radiation (low probability of intercept- LPI) for radar, and the possibility of creation of antiLPI passive radar are also discussed.

articleTitle: Radar images of the covered trenches FDTD simulation
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Results of computer simulation of the video pulse electromagnetic wave scattering in the media containing a dielectric insertion of rectangular or trapezoidal form imitating the backfilled trenches are presented. The finite difference time domain (FDTD) method and the second-order Mur absorbing boundary condition are used for the task solving. Radar images of rectangular form trenches have been analyzed in dependence on depth and width of the trench and on the spacing between the sounding field source and observation point (in other words on the separation between the transmitting and receiving antennas of the GPR). It is ascertained common properties, typical for the radar images of all type of trenches and individual properties typical only for the trenches either, one or another type. It is investigated distinctions of the radar images.

articleTitle: Radiation of impulse-like waveforms with illustrative applications
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: We start this work with a discussion of what is ultra wideband. A related issue is the classification of high-power electromagnetic (HPEM) waveforms. Four ways of classifying HPEM signals based on bandwidth that has been recently proposed is described in detail. An antenna system that radiates impulse-like waveforms making use of paraboloidal reflectors has been called the impulse radiating antennas (IRA) and is an excellent example of a hyperband system. The paper also describes some examples of such antennas and potential applications.

articleTitle: Restoration of reflectogram by extrapolation wideband microwave measurements by method of minimum duration
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Problems of reflectogram restoration and autocorrelation function of reflectogram restorations are considered. The method of minimum duration is modified for cases of spectra extrapolation onto lower and higher frequencies. Optimal values of work parameters of "generalized" functional of duration are found. Results of numeric simulation are presented for one-layered dielectric structure.

articleTitle: Neural recognition of aerial target types using a high range resolution radar
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The combination of the least mean squares and back propagation training procedures for the ANN training is considered on the example task of recognition between 11 types of aerial objects using a high range resolution radar (HRR radar) allowing to obtain single range profiles (RP) or trains of RPs. Results of simulation are presented.

articleTitle: The antenna systems synthesis according to the amplitude characteristics under condition of electromagnetic compatibility
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The synthesis problems for two types of antennas are considered on the additional requirement of the electromagnetic compatibility. The variational statement of the synthesis problems consists in minimization of functional presented the mean-square deviation of the prescribed and synthesized amplitude radiation patterns together with additional summand that allows to minimize the field values in a near zone. The other functional allows to maximize the front-to-rear factor in the given range of frequencies and to minimize it outside of this range. The solutions of analysis problems are presented in explicit notation or as series of computing procedures that to a considerable degree simplifies the process of solving the synthesis problems.

articleTitle: Advantages of the wideband and ultra wideband signals in the remote sensing
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Some aspects of the wideband and ultrawideband signals usage considered. Essential aspects of the processing techniques as well as models of the input process represented and discussed. The term efficiency bandwidth and principle of the waveform selection represented. Concept of the wideband signals in the synthetic aperture radar presented. Results which show advantages of these signals are shown.

articleTitle: The influence of microwaves with different state of polarization on the state of chromatin and viability of drosophila
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Microwave radiation of different polarization state of wavelength 7.1 mm (f=42.25 GHz) and surface power density at the level of an object - 0.2 mW/cm/sup 2/, exposure time 10 min. induces condensation of chromatin in human buccal cell nuclei. The effect of chromatin condensation was also observed after the influence of irradiation produced by cell phone. Microwave radiation induced the decrease of reproductive ability of drosophila. Left polarized microwave radiation induced more pronounced effects on chromatin condensation in human cells and reproductive ability of drosophila than right polarized microwave radiation.

articleTitle: A compact testing chamber for the experimental proving-researches of the wideband space-vehicle antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The radiation-aperture characteristics are investigated in a wide band 2-15 GHz in both near and far zones. The optimum distances between the investigated antenna, a collimation mirror, and the collimation mirror irradiator of the compact testing chamber for antennas are determined. The main features of the collimation mirror and the compact testing chamber are presented.

articleTitle: Application of the audio interface for ground penetrating radar data representation and interpretation
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The present article offers a description of software complex, which supports reception and preliminary processing of ground penetrating radar (GPR) information, development of flag description, generation of radar displays and synthesis of their audio representation in the tasks of underground sounding data interpretation. A method of image-to-sound conversion is described, with the storage of image information at the level of attainable resolution. Technical feasibility of the replacement of visual perception with acoustic perception has been substantiated. Practical limitations of the parameters of conversion have been defined, and the conformity of the coded values with the level of perception of audio information has been verified.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic compatibility of rass techniques under the airfield conditions
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The solution of the electromagnetic compatibility problem for radioacoustic atmospheric sounding equipment in the airfield conditions by using a special quasicontinuous condition is discussed. Namely, the sounding acoustic parcels are illuminated with radio impulses of a triangular pulse envelope form, and the spatial fronts duration providing the coverage of the whole working height interval. In the sounding height interval of about 500 m, the active spectrum-width of radiated radio signals is only 0.34 MHz, i.e. approximately five times less than that of short rectangular radio pulses. The sounding height measurement is made via acoustic channel with the margin error not worse than 0.8 %, the sound pulse parcels spatial duration is 30 m. Such radioacoustic techniques can be placed in immediate proximity to a runway in order to control mesoscale weather phenomena, dangerous for aircraft.

articleTitle: A novel ultra-wideband offset-fed reflector antenna system with main lobe selection
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: We present results of research, development and tests of a novel ultra-wideband offset-fed reflector antenna system with main lobe selection for ultra-wideband radars with high resolution.

articleTitle: Influence of the curvilinear surface of diffractive optical elements of MM-wave and THz wave to dispersion distortion correction of femtosecond pulses
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Peculiarities of propagation of femtosecond pulses through a focusing diffractive optical element of millimeter wave are considered. It is shown that the time delay between the pulse and phase wavefronts can be decreased by fabricating the diffractive optical element on the optimal curvilinear surface.

articleTitle: Attenuation and phase shift of 6-mm electromagnetic wave with wide frequency band in watering medium
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Description of experimental facilities for measurements of attenuation and phase shift in raining water formation is presented. The experimental technique is based on multifrequency wideband measurements with synthesis of signal of spatial distribution of reflection along longitudinal axis. The multifrequency measurements and synthesis have been done in real-time. The apparatus consists of modules of scalar reflectometer of series P2 (R2). The desired information is extracted from the amplitude and position of the peak of reflection from metal plate fixed beyond the zone of water raining. Some results of experimental investigation of physical model of raining medium are presented.

articleTitle: Based on two-port network theory simulation of electromagnetic wave propagation in multilayer medium
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The simulation program for analysis of impulse electromagnetic wave propagation in multilayer medium providing to take into account the frequency dependence of electrophysical parameters of layers (dispersion) was developed based on two-port network theory.

articleTitle: The modification of radiation characteristics in Fresnel antenna
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The general approach to analysis of sounded Fresnel antenna is considered. The frequency characteristics of Fresnel antenna are analyzed. The radiation characteristics of Fresnel antenna are considered.

articleTitle: Pulse plane wave diffraction on a curvilinear impedance wedge: UAT analysis
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The work deals with the problem of plane wave diffraction on a wedge with curvilinear impedance faces. The solution is obtained in the form of the geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) Keller J. B. (1962) and its uniform extension uniform asymptotic theory (UAT) Borovikov V. A. et al. (1978). V.M. Babich and V.S. Buldyrev uniform formulas (1972) are used for the field evaluation in the shadow region. Numerical results are obtained for the case of the incident Gaussian pulse.

articleTitle: The package of programs for solving model initial boundary-value problems in the theory of nonsinusoidal electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The package of programs for solving a wide range of two-dimensional problems in the theory of transient electromagnetic fields is presented. This pattern contains all the styles that should be used in the paper. The detailed instructions are presented in This work.

articleTitle: Transient electromagnetic fields in unbounded space with inhomogeneous medium
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: To solve propagation problems in time domain directly the modal representation of transient electromagnetic fields is considered. Using evolutionary approach the initial nonstationary three-dimensional electrodynamic problem is transformed into the problem for the system of connected one-dimensional evolutionary equations. The system describes the interconversions of all modes on inhomogeneities in cross-section. After elimination of the longitudinal components of electrical and magnetic field from Maxwell equation system the four-dimensional differential operators are formed. It is proved that the operators are self-adjoint ones. The completeness of the basis is proved by means of Weyl theorem about orthogonal splitting of Hilbert space. The expansion coefficients of transient electromagnetic field can be found from the set of evolutionary equations.

articleTitle: MC-generators for upper atmosphere investigations
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The results of testing of miniature explosive sources intended for researches of physical processes in the upper atmosphere, occurring under influence of a powerful electromagnetic signal are represented.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of the narrowband and wideband methods of target recognition
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Results of comparative study of radar recognition with the use of narrowband and wideband signals as well as various recognition signatures are presented. The advantage of wideband radar signals is emphasized. The results show that use of wideband signals allow increasing the accuracy of radar measurements and radar immunity against interference providing the same detection range.

articleTitle: Absorbing and scattering of a short pulses radiation by the radioabsorbing materials
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Here are the results of experimental researches by pulse signal of the absorbing-and diffusing material "Contrast". The material is effective for wideband signals and may be used for camouflaging in the radio-location.

articleTitle: On the construction of problem-specific bases, frames, and wavelets in computational electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The adequate analysis (transform) and synthesis (inverse transform) of functions (signals) in Hilbert space critically determine the overall performance of large-scale modeling and simulation of real-life problems in computational electromagnetics. Thereby, numerical schemes supporting the multiresolution and multiscale analysis lead to particularly well-structured and efficient formulations. This contribution is an attempt to further popularize some of the strikingly beautiful insights and enabling methodologies, which have been developing in the harmonic- and nonharmonic analysis community, among the scientists and engineers active in computational electromagnetics. The notions of orthogonal bases, nonorthogonal bases, dual bases, frames, and dual frames are briefly reviewed and presented in a unified fashion. It is shown that the spectral-domain far-field asymptotic tails of Green's functions associated with electromagnetic wave propagation problems can be utilized to create finite-support orthogonal wavelets, satisfying the axioms of the multiresolution analysis.

articleTitle: Advancing of electromagnetic waves through nonlinear film in the microwave receiver antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Nonlinear boundary conditions were first used in Shifrin Y. S. et al. (2003). After that, the integral equation construction for research antennas became possible. Works on the propagation plane strong waves in the nonlinear half space were generalized in [Landau L. P. et al., (1982), p.531-534]. Boundary conditions for the dielectric and magnetic permeability have /spl epsiv/(E) and /spl mu/(H), were constructed. Thus, the decisive propagation task became relatively simple. The possibilities of utilization of these conditions are considered here for: a) different nonlinear types of film; b) arbitrary direction of incident wave.

articleTitle: Recognition capability experimental estimation of soft objects with radiometric systems
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: There are offered the results of quantitative estimation of detection possibilities with following identification of soft objects which are obtained on basis of analysis of 2D-radiometric images.

articleTitle: The time delay effect on the pulse radiation of a tapered slot antenna array
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The former of impulses is described on the basis of generators with steerable time delay in This work. The pulse radiation of TSA array was simulated numerically. In experiment the former consists of two generators of video pulses, of the power supply and the control unit. The generators nominal amplitude is about 300 V. The electronic regulator in the control unit provides delaying.

articleTitle: A concise UTD formulation for the scattering by a wedge with impedance faces
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: A concise formulation of the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) solution for the scattering by a wedge with isotropic impedance faces at a plane wave normally incident case is deduced in This work, which inherits the uniformity of the original result, overcomes the complexity of the former, expresses clearly physical meanings, and is very prone to calculation with computer. The numerical results agree well with those given by published papers.

articleTitle: Scattering pulse signal on layer-uniform half-space
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The problem of a plane pulse wave scattering of on the layer-uniform half-space with arbitrary complex dielectric permittivities of layers is considered. The proposal method bases on the boundary problem solution for the system of stationary Maxwell equations and well adapted to determination of complex amplitudes of the fields at any point of space.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations and analysis of the diffraction problem on the nonlinear dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: On an example of the open nonlinear electrodynamic system-transverse nonhomogeneous, isotropic, nonmagnetic, linearly polarized, nonlinear (a Kerr-like dielectric nonlinearity) dielectric layer, the algorithms of solution of the diffraction problem of a plane wave on the nonlinear object and the results of the numerical analysis of the nonlinear problem are shown. The nonlinear diffraction problem reduced the solutions of the system of the nonhomogeneous nonlinear equations of the second kind. The first of algorithm based on the iterative scheme on the basis of Simpson's quadrature is applicable to the solution of the nonlinear equations system. The following algorithms are based on the Newtonian method for the Simpson's quadrature and the Newtonian algorithm for the Teilor-series of the diffraction field.

articleTitle: Spatial forming of super broadband outgoing signals
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The traditional tendency of broadband pulses forming is in using one or more high-capacity relativistic generator Panov V. V. et al. (1993). Due to the elemental base development of solid-state active modules PAA which allow to manage the phase and frequency of outgoing pulses to high precision and the opportunity to create multifrequency active antenna arrays (MFAAA).

articleTitle: Dispersion by periodic screens of broadband electromagnetic pulses
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Research of dispersion on the planar periodical grating of the amplitude-modulated pulses of any duration has been considered by the numerical analysis of spectral functions of scattered field and integrated representations of studying fields. From calculated curves the parameters of planar periodical grating, at which the scattered signal possesses the maximal distortions as the decreasing of amplitude, appearing of group delay and increasing of effective duration, are determined. The behavior of pulses on various distances from a periodic grating is considered.

articleTitle: High-resolution radars at the Institute of radio astronomy of the NAS of Ukraine
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: A review is given of recent activities undertaken in the Institute of radio astronomy of the National academy of sciences of Ukraine for the development of high-resolution radars. The radars developed include 95 and 36 GHz cloud radars and an airborne, K/sub u/-band SAR radar system. They are capable to perform real-time, high-resolution measurements. The set-up of these instruments, the novel technical solutions, and the signal processing technique introduced are discussed. The results obtained with such instruments during measurement campaigns are presented as well.

articleTitle: The numerical methods for the analysis of the diffraction problems of an electromagnetic field by a wavy interface
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Numerical methods are proposed for solving problems of reflection of a plane electromagnetic wave from an irregular media interface. Strictly transparent periodic cylindrical surfaces are considered, as well as surfaces that are no-planar on a finite impedance section. The method of integral equations is used to construct numerical algorithms. Integral characteristics of the electromagnetic field and the current distribution at the interface are investigated. Single- and multimode scattered fields are considered. Numerical results are reported for various electrodynamic models, and their limits of applicability are investigated.

articleTitle: Study and design of an intelligent acoustic-waves-monitor based on acoustic emission
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: To improve the mining reliability, an intelligent acoustic-waves-monitor is developed to use for monitoring the stability of rock. This paper introduces the principle figure of an intelligent acoustic-waves-monitor based on acoustic emission, and describes its software design, hardware design and some parts of functions. Practical use shows that it can provide numeric and graphic data for technical persons, and provide a reliable tool for mines to evaluate the safety of producing

articleTitle: Nonperiodical wideband signals in synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: In the synthetic aperture radars periodical signals (usually radiopulses with the rectangular envelope) are used. This leads to ambiguity measurements which must be eliminated by varying different parameters of the SAR. In this paper we consider usage of the nonperiodical signals to avoid ambiguity measurements in synthetic aperture radars. Examples of the processing algorithm simplification are represented

articleTitle: Exploration of icy crust on Europa satellite by means of radiometer
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: In this work, we analyze one electrodynamic model of the crust considering a two layered crust. The purpose is to obtain the optimal electrophysical parameters of measurement that permit us to estimate the crust thickness. These parameters are calculated from the inverse elements of the Fisher matrix. The results obtained from this work can be used to plan future space missions. The optimal algorithms for these measurements can be modified to be used in active systems of remote sensing.

articleTitle: Application of the nanosecond pulses in scientific researches
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The paper is on the effect of the powerful nanosecond electromagnetic impulses as regards physical-chemical properties of substances. The changes of water properties of aqueous solutions of salts and melts of metals under the nanosecond electromagnetic impulses are outlined. Certain experiments which can be interpreted as due to a transmutation of the chemical elements are presented.

articleTitle: Principles of designing of optocontrolled antennas for wideband radiolocation systems
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental researches on optocontrolled antennas for wideband radiolocation systems with coherent optical devices of information processing and filtration are presented.

articleTitle: Increase of efficiency of suppression of reflecting from handicaps (interferences) such as "angel-echo" at the expense of use of multifrequency signals
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Problems of increase of efficiency of selection of handicaps (interferences) such as the "angel-echo", overloading a receiving (an acceptance) channel of the radar station of seaside referencing surveyed, performances of these handicaps (interferences) are parsed and the method of their selection suppression is offered at the expense of use of multifrequency signals.

articleTitle: The analysis of the matching opportunity of the parameters of the wideband through ionosphere signals with real dispersion radio line
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Concept of active mastering and constructive use of dispersive deforming properties of the transmitting environment which are limiting accuracy, carrying and resolution of broadband radio-electronic systems, for example, communication, location, navigation (including global) are first worked out in This work.

articleTitle: Nonequilibrium thermodynamic model semiconductor radioisotope coverings in view of quantum statistics
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: In This work, nonequilibrium thermodynamic model is proposed. The semiconductor radioisotope coverings with the generalized Boltzmann kinetic equation for the system in view of quantum statistics are studied. The introduced thermodynamic model incorporates the physical system with the source and the sinks being independent of the specific potentials of interactions in the system. The paper considers the approach of the nonGibbs distributions in the system thermodynamics, for which the entropy basic property is nonextensiveness.

articleTitle: Recognition of objects on their complex natural resonance at ultra wideband sounding
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: In this report, the RSO (radar subsurface objects) complex resonance frequencies are used as features of their recognition proposed. From these features the basis of the prior information about identifiable object scattering characteristics is described. However, for practical implementation of described algorithm of RSO recognition it is necessary to explore and to take into account effect of some complicating factors such as deformation of observed data. Thus from this report the algorithm of recognition of RSO is designed.

articleTitle: A powerful meter-wave pulse power source
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The results of the experimental investigation of the output characteristics of a pulse microwave power source made up as two modules on the powerful bipolar transistors are presented. The source allows to obtain on a matched load Z/sub L/=50 /spl Omega/ the pulse power P/sub out,i//spl sim/1 kW (carrier frequency f=150 MHz; pulse duration /spl tau//sub i/=0.5 ms; pulse frequency F/sub i/ = 10 Hz).

articleTitle: Intensity of the field and resonant scattering of the waves by nonlinear dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The open nonlinear electrodynamic system-transverse nonhomogeneous, isotropic, nonmagnetic, linearly polarized, nonlinear (a Kerr-like dielectric nonlinearity) dielectric layer is considered. The results of the numerical analysis of the diffraction problem of a plane wave on the nonlinear object are shown. Results of calculations in area frequency and intensity of inciting field the following. The effect of nonuniform shift of resonant frequency of the diffraction characteristics of a nonlinear dielectric layer (reduction of value of resonant frequency with increase and reduction of a steepness of the diffraction characteristics before and after resonant frequency) is found out at increase of intensity of inciting field. At calculations in area of various angle and intensity of inciting field the effect of increase of the angle of the transparency of the nonlinear layer at growth of intensity of the field is found out.

articleTitle: The strobe pulse shaper built on strip line shielded by ferrite
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The present work deals with the investigation of the pulse shaper based on a shorted symmetrical strip line. It has been determined that the best balancing and minimum afterpulse oscillations are provided in the pulse shaper where at first short pulses are formed and then balancing of the output signal is performed. The best strobe pulse shaper is a shaper with ferrite that has a larger relative permeability. The suitable design of the line-balance converter for the 100 ps strobe pulse shaping was obtained.

articleTitle: Monotonous difference schemes for the Maxwell equations in the problem of nonstationary wave diffraction by double periodic arrays
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: A new difference scheme is constructed by using the flow form of the Maxwell equations for the solution of three-dimensional time-dependent problem of plane electromagnetic wave diffraction by planar periodic on two directions structure consisted of metal strip particles. The limiting principle is applied to increasing of algorithm efficiency. Some field characteristics are obtained in the problems of wave diffraction by periodic arrays of strip dipoles and C-shaped volumetric particles.

articleTitle: The use of the monopulse type antenna system in GPR for increasing accuracy of horizontal coordinate measurement
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The possibility to increase accuracy of horizontal coordinate measurement of the local near surface object by means of using the monopulse type antenna system is presented. The basic principles of designing such an antenna are discussed. It is shown that if the receiving (or transmitting) unit is placed in the center of the antenna system there is a possibility to form in the symmetry plane an electromagnetic field with zero amplitude or absence of signal reflected from the object located in the symmetry plane owing to symmetry of antenna system and inverse driving of the antenna elements. It is proposed to use this phenomenon to increase accuracy of GPR measurements. Experimental GPR data illustrate high contrast of radar image of the object if these data are acquired by GPR with monopulse type antenna system. Such a design of the antenna system provides high electrodynamic isolation between the transmitting and receiving units of antenna system

articleTitle: Wideband signals processing with atomic functions in antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The new method of wideband signals processing on the basis of the theory of atomic functions (AF) in the complex antenna systems is offered. Efficiency of a method by the example of the decision of two problems: detection of the target and approximation of distribution of a current in the linear antenna is shown. Comparison with known approaches to the given problem is carried out.

articleTitle: Analysis of near-field radiation from an open-ended rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: On the basis of Hertz's potentials technique the radiation characteristics in near and intermediate zones of single mode and oversize rectangular waveguides have been investigated. The bounds of far-field zone have been determined for small in comparison with wavelength waveguide radiators. For these small radiators the classical expressions for far-zone can be applied. The influence of the effects of electromagnetic mode reflection and transformation at the antenna aperture on radiation characteristics in near-zone has been analyzed

articleTitle: Some aspects of usage of the pseudo noise sequences in the radiolocation systems
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Pseudo noise sequences (Barker's codes, M sequences etc.) widely use in communication and navigation systems. But for nowadays this kind of signals almost has no application in the radiolocation systems. This work investigates aspects of usage of pseudo noise sequences (PNS) in the radiolocation systems, some aspects of generating and processing of the input processes. Main emphasis was made on signal-to-noise ratio behaviour in the systems with pseudonoise signals in comparison with classic radiolocators.

articleTitle: Methods of the measurement of ultrashort impulse signals
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Here consider methods of the building of measuring channels electrics and magnetic component of pulsed electromagnetic fields. Cite an instance their concrete practical realization.

articleTitle: The development of methods of the improvement of the metrological characteristics of high-sensitivity MM-range radiometric equipment
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The development of methods of the improvement of the metrological characteristics of high-sensitivity MM-range radiometric equipment is proposed in This work. The electromagnetic radiation of biological objects, inclusive of the humans, has been actively studied. Diagnostics of the state of an organism is carried out proceeding from the values of radiation parameters. Thus they allow us to reach the higher accuracy and by the removal of preliminary microwave amplifier at quadrature detector input substantially expands the reception band of a radiometer and reduces the fluctuation threshold of sensitivity.

articleTitle: Multifrequency introscopy of 6-mm wave range with Fourier-transformation in spatial domain: a horn antenna resolution and properties
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Description of a microwave introscope combining multifrequency measurements and transversal scanning is presented. Longitudinal distance dependencies of reflectivity are obtained by synthesis from multifrequency data. The multifrequency measurements and synthesis is done in real-time. The apparatus carries out the measurements in free space. It is assembled using measuring modules of scalar reflectometer of series P2 (R2). Combination of data in longitudinal and transversal directions produces radio images of dielectric structures with embedded objects. A horn antenna as a probe is used. Some results of transversal resolution as function of distance and estimation of domain for correct determination of parameters structure are presented.

articleTitle: On radiation efficiency and radiating capability of impulse antennas
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Electromagnetic radiation efficiency and radiating capability of impulse antenna are discussed at This work. A term of impulse antenna is referred to an electromagnetic pulse radiation system with short pulse response. Relation between such antenna characteristics as storage factor, efficiency and radiating capability is considered here. Improvement methods of impulse antenna efficiency and radiating capability are discussed also. Possibilities of impulse antenna efficiency improvement with high radiating efficiency preservation are discussed. It is shown that efficiency of impulse and resonant antennas may be commensurable if energy recuperation back into power supply is provided. Some methods to increase impulse antenna efficiency and radiating capability are described and discussed.

articleTitle: Signal processing techniques at radar measurement of the UWB polarization characteristics
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: In the report the principles of processing of the UWB signals for an estimation of frequency responses polarization matrices by results of measurements are discussed. The reviewed methods are introduced in a "TSUNAMl-3" collimating type radar measuring complex. The outcomes of obtaining 2D polarization object radar images on experimental data are resulted.

articleTitle: Pulse scattering by printed-circuit discontinuities
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Gaussian pulse scattering by the microstrip gap and the microstrip T-junction is simulated based on the finite-difference time-domain method. Time-domain results are obtained and visualized to explicitly illustrate pulse scattering. Frequency-domain characteristics of the discontinuities in terms of scattering matrix coefficients are derived from the Fourier-transformed time-domain data. The results of calculations are compared with other available data.

articleTitle: Problems and promising lines of development of UWB ground penetrating radiolocation
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Some problems existing in modern UWB ground penetrating radiolocation are analyzed. Possible ways of further development of GPR engineering are discussed. Approaches to a problem of primary radar data improvement are proposed.

articleTitle: Field of the pulsed space-time source in simulated medium
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Rigorous studying of transfer of energy and behaviour of a wavefront in simulated fractal medium is based on application of new differintegral model of a space-time source. The relations featuring behaviour are considered /spl alpha/-form of wave packets, the wavefronts produced by a pulsed source.

articleTitle: Simulation of the automodulation effects in a chain of Gunn diodes with time delays
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Self-oscillations in a chain of Gunn diodes connected by sections of transmission line have been simulated. Simulations are compared with analytical considerations developed for a single-diode circuit with a stub or with no stub.

articleTitle: About the possibility of increasing of noise defended radio-wave radar at application of the "short" signal
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The purpose of the article is the decision of a problem of increasing of quality characteristic radio-wave radar. The method of the "short" signal is given. One of ways of increasing of quality indicators radio-wave radar is increasing energy potential of radio-wave radar: 1) increasing potential of a probing signal; 2) increasing radars length.

articleTitle: RF source of nanosecond pulsed electron beam with driving plasma cathode
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The paper describes results of the experimental research of generation of intense pulsed electron beam in S-band RF gun with driven plasma cathode. There has been designed experimental sample of the cathode based on ferroelectric ceramics. It has been obtained at RF gun output electron beam with particle energy /spl cong/500 keV, pulsed peak current of 3 A and pulse duration of 50 ns.

articleTitle: Pulse-and continuous-mode generators of mm-range on GaAs Gunn-diodes
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The design of wideband mm-band generators in the way of waveguide, coaxial waveguide, and microstrip patterns is considered. The power, frequency and temperature characteristics of the proposed generators are investigated experimentally and theoretically. As the active elements of the generators are used GaAs Gunn-diodes; those developed and made of the chair of semiconductor and vacuum electronics of Karazin KHNU, and the industrial production GaAs Gunn-diodes as well.

articleTitle: The solving of ecological monitoring task with microwave
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Microwave technique and device for the measurements of refraction coefficients in different layers pollution of atmosphere surface near the plant with phase radar methods are presented. Uncertainty elimination of the phase measurements is discussed and one is achieved by frequency changing upon certain rule. That gives increasing of measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: Novel effective technique for time-domain electromagnetic simulation
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The approaches considered are oriented to substantial reduction of the resources required for solving complex 'open' electrodynamic problems and, at the same time, to the reliability growth of the calculated data. We are dealing with the great improvements-by an order and higher. Our expectations are confirmed by specific results. The approaches are fully studied analytically: today their implementation (in software and in various physical investigations) is easily understood for well trained students and for everybody who look upon mathematical modeling and numerical experiment as being efficient tools for gaining new knowledge.

articleTitle: Spatial and power characteristics of the ultrawideband reflector
publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The electrodynamic method of calculation the spatial-temporary characteristics of large electrical sizes mirror antennas with the help of integrated representations for the surface current density is offered with account of conditions on the edge in the Meixner's form. The settlement power characteristics used for determining potentialities of radar-tracking processing of an accepted signal are given in the work.

publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members.

publicationTitle: 2004 Second International Workshop Ultrawideband and Ultrashort Impulse Signals (IEEE Cat. No.04EX925)
abstract: The 2004 Second International Workshop "Ultrawideband and Ultrashot Impulse Signals" is dedicated to 200-anniversary of V.N. Karazin Kharkov National University. A brief history of the university is provided.
